name: swedish-provincial-symbols

description.en: The provincial flowers (landskapsblommor) and provincial animals (landskapsdjur) of Sweden's 25 provinces: 50 cards. Front: the province, under its Swedish name (Skåne = Scania, Lappland = Lapland), and the symbol, e.g. "Uppland: provincial flower"; back: the plant or animal in English and Swedish, with its scientific name in a note. The flowers go back to a list of 1908; Blekinge, Dalarna, Härjedalen and Medelpad have two plants in use, and their cards give both. The animals were announced in 1988 after a public vote that WWF Sweden ran in 1987. From Wikidata, Dyntaxa and Wikipedia, checked against WWF Sweden and the Swedish Museum of Natural History.
description.sv: Landskapsblommorna och landskapsdjuren för Sveriges 25 landskap: 50 kort. Framsida: landskapet och symbolen, t.ex. ”Uppland: landskapsblomma”; baksida: växten eller djuret på engelska och svenska, med det vetenskapliga namnet i en anteckning. Blommorna går tillbaka på en lista från 1908; Blekinge, Dalarna, Härjedalen och Medelpad har två växter i bruk, och deras kort anger båda. Djuren tillkännagavs 1988 efter en folkomröstning som Världsnaturfonden WWF anordnade 1987. Uppgifterna kommer från Wikidata, Dyntaxa och Wikipedia och är kontrollerade mot WWF och Naturhistoriska riksmuseet.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (Dyntaxa through the GBIF API, live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

1. Provincial flowers from Wikidata (query 1): every P2238 (official symbol) statement on the instances of province of Sweden (Q193556), with its P3831 (object of statement has role) qualifier, rank, taxon name and English and Swedish labels. All 29 statements have the role landskapsblommor (Q7252554) and normal rank; they cover the 25 provinces, Blekinge, Dalarna, Härjedalen and Medelpad with two plants each. (Wikidata has two items that are instances of Q193556 for Södermanland; only Q626062 has P2238 statements.) Wikidata has no statements for the provincial animals.

2. Names from Wikidata (queries 2 and 3): the P225 (taxon name), the English, Swedish and multilingual labels and aliases and the P1843 (taxon common name) values of all the plants and animals (query 2 reads the truthy wdt: values, so where one value has preferred rank the normal-rank values are not returned; the evidence on the cards says "truthy values", and query 12 lists all ranks for the animals), and the labels and aliases of the provinces. The animals' items were found through the Swedish Wikipedia articles linked from its "Landskapsdjur" table (query 6, pageprops wikibase_item); the link "Älg" leads to the article on the genus (Q10731891), so the species item moose (Q35517, Alces alces) was found with the Wikidata search API and its names fetched with query 3.

3. Dyntaxa (query 4): the script dyntaxa.py looked up every scientific name in the Dyntaxa checklist as published on GBIF (dataset version of 29 September 2026), kept the entries whose canonical name matches the scientific name exactly (no fuzzy or partial matches), followed each to its accepted taxon (the acceptedKey of a synonym), and fetched the Swedish (and English) vernacular names of the accepted taxon. All 54 names are accepted except Trientalis europaea, which Dyntaxa lists as a synonym of Lysimachia europaea.

4. Provincial animals from the Swedish Wikipedia (query 5): the wikitext of "Landskapsdjur" and "Landskapsblommor" (with the overview "Svenska landskapssymboler") was fetched through the MediaWiki API with revision ids; rows.py extracted the table row of each province, which is quoted on the cards. The animals' list is checked against WWF Sweden's own page on the 1987–1988 vote (query 8), which lists the same 25 animals, and five of them against Skogen i skolan's lesson plan (query 9).

5. Flowers cross-checked against the Swedish Museum of Natural History's Den virtuella floran (query 7): the live page answered 404, so the Wayback Machine's copy of 2 December 2021 was read. It gives one plant per province and says its choice follows Nationalencyklopedin; for the four provinces with two plants it gives the oak (Blekinge), the spreading bellflower (Dalarna), the spring pasqueflower (Härjedalen) and the Norway spruce (Medelpad). It agrees with Wikidata on the other 21 provinces. It is not fully independent of the Swedish Wikipedia, whose "Andra förslag" column cites Den virtuella floran for most entries; for the flowers, the independent checks of that column are Wikidata, the table's 1908 column and the English Wikipedia list. Wittrock's 1908 list, as quoted in six notes, was checked against Bergianska trädgården's history page (query 14), which gives "Hälsningland: Tall" where the Swedish Wikipedia table's 1908 column wrongly gives lin. The Swedish and English Wikipedia lists (queries 5 and 10) agree with Wikidata on all 25 provinces, including the two plants of the four provinces.

6. English names: the English name is a label, alias or P1843 value of the plant's or animal's Wikidata item where one has the form used (lower case except proper names such as Norway, Arctic, Eurasian, Siberian). Where Wikidata or Dyntaxa gives the name only in title case (e.g. "Siberian Jay", "Western capercaillie", "Mountain Hare", "Hazel dormouse"), the card uses it in sentence case, keeping capitals only for proper names (Eurasian, Siberian, Arctic, Atlantic); this applies to animal-norrbotten, animal-gastrikland, animal-medelpad, animal-narke, animal-vasterbotten, animal-vastergotland, animal-ostergotland, animal-dalarna and animal-angermanland, whose names the truthy Wikidata values or Dyntaxa give in that form apart from case (common crane, mute swan and Eurasian beaver are also normal-rank P1843 values in exactly the card's form, query 12). Otherwise the card uses the name given in the introduction of the English Wikipedia article on the plant or animal (queries 10 and 13), quoted on the card. Species are named with the qualified species name (common honeysuckle, common ivy, European mistletoe, common raven), not a name that also covers the genus. Swedish names: the Dyntaxa Swedish name, all of which are also given by the Swedish Wikipedia and NRM lists; Blekinge's oak is "ek" (Dyntaxa lists "skogsek" and "ek"; every list of provincial flowers says "ek") and Medelpad's globeflower "smörboll" (Dyntaxa lists "smörbollar" and "smörboll"; the lists say "smörboll").

7. Cards: cards.py built the 50 cards from the saved data and an editorial table (province, plant or animal items, English and Swedish names, notes), quoting each source's own row or statement as evidence, and generated the Wikidata checks: the province's Swedish and English label or alias, each P2238 statement, each P225 value, and the English and Swedish name wherever Wikidata has it exactly as on the card (label, alias or P1843). dossier.py added the evidence for the notes and the metadata. Fronts: "<province>: provincial flower" / "<province>: landskapsblomma" and "<province>: provincial animal" / "<province>: landskapsdjur", with the provinces under their Swedish names in both languages (Wikidata's English aliases include "Skåne" and "Lappland"). The four provinces with two flowers have the front note "two plants are named" and both plants on the back, the one in Wittrock's 1908 list first. Every back note gives the scientific name, written as part of the English and Swedish note text.
selection: One provincial flower card and one provincial animal card for each of Sweden's 25 provinces (landskap): 50 cards. Flowers: the plants Wikidata records as each province's official symbol in the role landskapsblommor, which match the Swedish and English Wikipedia lists and, for 21 provinces, Den virtuella floran; for Blekinge, Dalarna, Härjedalen and Medelpad, where two plants are in use and no list settles which, the card names both. Animals: the 25 landskapsdjur chosen in 1987–1988 by a jury after WWF Sweden's public vote, as listed by the Swedish Wikipedia and by WWF Sweden. Left out: the many other provincial symbols (birds, fish, insects, fungi, mosses, stones, apples and so on, most of them chosen by private societies), county (län) symbols, Sweden's national flower (liten blåklocka, chosen in a 2021 vote) and the older choices of Wittrock's 1908 list that are no longer used (they appear in notes where they explain a card).

Den virtuella floran (Swedish Museum of Natural History), Bergianska trädgården, WWF Sweden and Skogen i skolan were used for verification only: they confirmed facts the content sources gave, and no wording, layout or selection was copied from them. The fronts and notes are the compiler's own wording.

rounds.summary: All sources agree on the provincial animal of every province and on the flower of 21 provinces; four provinces have two plants in use and their cards give both. Two scientific or Swedish names were corrected against Dyntaxa (Lysimachia europaea; äkta förgätmigej). No Wikidata check was skipped because Wikidata disagreed with a better source in substance; checks are absent only where Wikidata's capitalisation differs or it has no name in that form.

findings.issue: The brief for this deck gave Uppland's provincial flower as liverleaf (blåsippa). Every source consulted gives the snake's head fritillary (kungsängslilja, Fritillaria meleagris): Wikidata, Den virtuella floran, both Wikipedias (Wittrock's 1908 list included).
findings.resolution: The card gives the snake's head fritillary.

findings.issue: Four provinces have two plants in use. Wikidata (P2238), the English Wikipedia list and the Swedish Wikipedia ("Andra förslag" and its introduction) give both; Den virtuella floran, which follows Nationalencyklopedin, gives one: Blekinge oak (not great mullein), Dalarna spreading bellflower (not harebell), Härjedalen spring pasqueflower (not alpine yellow-violet), Medelpad Norway spruce (not globeflower). Wittrock's 1908 list has the oak, the harebell, the alpine yellow-violet and the spruce.
findings.resolution: No single list settles these four, so their cards say "two plants are named" on the front and give both plants on the back, the 1908 choice first, with a note on the alternative (flower-blekinge, flower-dalarna, flower-harjedalen, flower-medelpad). The description says so.

findings.issue: Wittrock's 1908 list differs from today's lists for Skåne (beech) and Hälsingland (Scots pine), changed in 1909 to the oxeye daisy and flax, and names other plants for Bohuslän (skogskaprifol), Halland (ginst), Värmland (duvkulla/skogsstjärna), Västerbotten (kungsspira) and Öland (storsippa/tovsippa).
findings.resolution: The cards follow the current lists, on which all sources agree; the Skåne and Hälsingland cards note the 1909 change. Skogskaprifol, ginst, duvkulla and kungsspira are older names or forms of the same plants; Öland's 1908 alternatives are not used by any current source.

findings.issue: Wikidata's item Q157581 has the taxon name Trientalis europaea (and that as its Swedish label); Dyntaxa lists Trientalis europaea as a synonym of Lysimachia europaea, as does the English Wikipedia ("Lysimachia europaea (formerly known as Trientalis europaea)").
findings.resolution: The note gives "Lysimachia europaea (formerly Trientalis europaea)"; the P225 check is left out for this card, since Wikidata's value is the older name; the P2238 check stays.

findings.issue: Wikidata's Swedish label is "förgätmigej"; Dyntaxa and Den virtuella floran call Myosotis scorpioides "äkta förgätmigej" ("förgätmigej" alone also names the genus).
findings.resolution: Back "äkta förgätmigej" / "true forget-me-not", the species' name.

findings.issue: Many Swedish labels in Wikidata begin with a capital ("Vildkaprifol", "Ängsklocka", "Hårginst", "Mosippa", "Fjällviol", "Kungsängslilja", "Kung Karls spira", "Styvmorsviol", "Ölandssolvända", "Knubbsäl"), Medelpad's globeflower is labelled "Smörbollar", and many English bird names are in title case ("Eurasian Eagle-owl", "Siberian Jay", "White-tailed Eagle" …); the builder's label checks are case-sensitive.
findings.resolution: The cards use Dyntaxa's lower-case Swedish names and sentence-case English names; a name check is made only where Wikidata has the name exactly as on the card (35 names have none; each is confirmed by Dyntaxa, Wikipedia or the NRM and WWF lists in the evidence). No check was dropped because Wikidata disagreed in substance.

findings.issue: The Swedish Wikipedia table links "Älg", which redirects to "Älgar", the article on the genus Alces (Q10731891).
findings.resolution: The card uses the species moose (Q35517, Alces alces), whose Swedish alias is "älg" and which Dyntaxa calls "älg"; WWF's list says "älg".

findings.issue: Wikidata's Swedish label for Salmo salar is "atlantlax" and for Castor fiber "europeisk bäver"; the WWF list, the Swedish Wikipedia table (link text) and Dyntaxa say "lax" and "bäver".
findings.resolution: Backs "lax" and "bäver" (animal-halland, animal-angermanland), without a Swedish name check.

findings.issue: The Swedish Wikipedia table shows a picture of Luscinia megarhynchos (the common nightingale) next to "Näktergal", but its link goes to the article on Luscinia luscinia, which Dyntaxa and Wikidata call näktergal (English: thrush nightingale).
findings.resolution: The card gives the thrush nightingale, Luscinia luscinia.

findings.issue: The bear won the vote in both Dalarna and Härjedalen; the jury gave it to Härjedalen, and Dalarna's animal is the Eurasian eagle-owl (Swedish Wikipedia, WWF).
findings.resolution: Noted on the Härjedalen card.

findings.issue: Wikidata's English label of Pandion haliaetus is "osprey" (lower case) while its P1843 value is "Osprey"; the card's English name is "osprey".
findings.resolution: The label check passes today; it is the only English form of this item that matches, so a change of the label's case would fail it and should be resolved by updating the check, not the card.

findings.issue: The Wikidata evidence presents the truthy (wdt:) P1843 values as if they were all of them; normal-rank values such as "white-tailed eagle"/"havsörn" (Q25438) and "osprey"/"fiskgjuse" (Q25332) are hidden by preferred-rank values, so round 0's statements on animal-sodermanland (the label being the only matching English form) and flower-bohuslan (no white-tailed eagle name in the card's form) are not true of Wikidata.

Round 0 is kept as written; this round corrects it: Wikidata does have "white-tailed eagle" and "osprey" as normal-rank P1843 values, but the builder's checks read truthy values only, so no check on them is possible while a preferred-rank value exists.
